title: Reading: Caesar, De Bello Gallico I.1
subtitle: Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs. The most famous opening sentence.
objectives: Read and translate Caesar's opening paragraph.
Recognize all grammatical forms in context.
Understand Caesar's direct, military prose style.

sections.heading: Caesar's opening
sections.body:
Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs, quārum ūnam incolunt Belgae, aliam Aquītānī, tertiam quī ipsōrum linguā Celtae, nostrā Gallī appellantur. Hī omnēs linguā, īnstitūtīs, lēgibus inter sē differunt. Gallōs ab Aquītānīs Garumna flūmen, ā Belgīs Mātrona et Sēquana dīvidit.

Gloss:
omnis — all, whole
dīvīdō, -ere, dīvīsī, dīvīsus — to divide
pars, partis (f.) — part
quārum — of which (gen. pl. fem.)
ūnus, -a, -um — one
incolō, -ere — to inhabit
alter, -a, -um — another, other
tertius, -a, -um — third
quī — who
ipse, -a, -um — self, themselves
linguā — language (abl. of means)
appellō, -āre — to call
hī — these
īnstitūtum, -ī (n.) — custom, institution
lēx, lēgis (f.) — law
inter sē — among themselves
differō, differre — to differ
flūmen, flūminis (n.) — river
dīvidō — separates

sections.heading: Translation guide
sections.body:
Gallia est omnis dīvīsa — Gaul is wholly divided (perfect passive participle + est forms perfect passive)
in partēs trēs — into three parts
quārum — of which (refers to 'parts')
ūnam incolunt Belgae — the Belgians inhabit one
aliam Aquītānī — the Aquitani (inhabit) another
tertiam quī... — a third (those) who...
ipsōrum linguā Celtae — in their own language Celts
nostrā Gallī appellantur — in ours (are) called Gauls

Read the paragraph aloud three times. Do not translate word-for-word. Let the rhythm emerge.

items.prompt: Into how many parts is Gaul divided?
What divides the Gauls from the Belgians?
What three things do these peoples differ in?

words.latin: Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs.
words.gloss: All Gaul is divided into three parts.
